MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Sep 18, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

Clarification of Funding for Gender-Affirming Care

Sep 18, 2026

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 13, 2026, that limits federal Medicaid and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) funding for certain gender-affirming medical care provided to minors, scheduled to take effect October 13, 2026. This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under 18 and CHIP enrollees under 19.  

The rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine law requires MaineCare to cover medically necessary treatment for or related to gender dysphoria and protects members from discrimination based on gender identity or gender expression.  

Providers should continue to provide these services as usual. Specific guidance for providers on Maine’s implementation of state-only coverage, including billing guidance, will be forthcoming.  

To help ensure MaineCare members receive the health care services they need, and have the information necessary to make informed decisions, OMS will continue to communicate with members about covered services through the Member Handbook and the OMS website.  

For questions, please contact Provider Relations Specialist, Lisa Bouchard.

Maine's Minimum Wage to Increase to $15.70 Per Hour in 2027

September 18, 2026

For Immediate Release: September 18, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor announced today that, effective January 1, 2027, the state minimum wage will increase from $15.10 to $15.70 per hour, based on data recently made available by the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics. MDOL is required under Maine law (Maine statute Title 26, chapter 7, section 664) to make annual adjustments to the minimum wage based on the cost-of-living index (CPI-W) for the Northeast Region, after Maine voters amended the law by referendum in 2016. Between August 2025 and August 2026, there was a 4.1 percent increase in the CPI-W.

According to the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Population Survey for 2025, there were 28,000 hourly workers who were paid less than $15.00 per hour. These workers represent about four percent of all wage and salary workers (both paid at hourly rates and not paid at hourly rates) and about eight percent of wage and salary workers who are paid at hourly rates.

Agricultural workers in Maine are also entitled to the state minimum wage, after the Legislature enacted and Governor Mills signed "An Act to Establish a State Minimum Hourly Wage for Agricultural Workers" in 2025.

The "tip wage," or service employee minimum wage, will increase from $7.55 to $7.85 per hour. This means that service employees must receive a direct cash wage of at least $7.85 per hour from the employer. The employer must be able to show that the employee receives at least the minimum wage of $15.70 per hour when the direct wage and tips are combined at the end of the week. The amount of tips necessary to qualify as a service employee will increase from $191 to $199 per month.

The minimum salary threshold for exempting a worker from overtime pay must exceed 3,000 times the State's minimum wage or the annualized rate established by the U.S. Department of Labor, whichever is higher. Starting January 1, 2027, the new minimum salary threshold for salaried workers exempt from overtime will be $905.79 per week, or $47,101.08 per year. This is only one of the factors used in determining whether a worker is exempt from overtime pay under federal or state law. An individual can earn more than the minimum salary threshold and still be eligible for overtime. The duties of each worker must be considered as part of this analysis.

Employers can download the required minimum wage poster at no cost on the Department's website.

The minimum wage and overtime law can be found here.

More information about minimum wage and other labor standards is available on the Department's website

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 21, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Sep 21, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 21, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles:   

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

  *As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines. 

Other system access limitations: 

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 21, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.  

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites New Jersey car wash for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards, proposes more than $446K in fines
entry.content: SICKLERVILLE, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a New Jersey car wash service for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards related to hazardous energy and excessive noise levels, proposing $446,864 in penalties.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that ModWash LLC, an express car wash service operating multiple locations throughout the country, including five in Sicklerville, willfully exposed workers to hazardous energy by failing to lock out equipment prior to conducting maintenance activities and not using energy control procedures. The agency also cited ModWash for two repeat violations for failing to have clear lockout procedures and specific instructions for controlling all energy sources and not training employees on equipment lockout/tagout processes. In addition, the employer was cited for five serious violations for failing to develop and implement a noise monitoring program, establish a baseline audiogram for employees within six months of exposure, train employees exposed to noise above 85 decibels, provide lockout/tagout devices, and attach such devices to machines prior to servicing them.The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Florida pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards after March fatality
entry.content: ORLANDO, FL – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an Orlando-based pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing employees to safety hazards after an incident claimed the life of a worker at a New Smyrna Beach worksite in March 2026.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that on March 17, 2026, T & T Pipeline Co. Inc. employees were replacing a drill bit on a horizontal drilling machine when the pipe stem began to rotate and fatally struck the employee.OSHA cited the employer with a willful violation for exposing employees to struck-by hazards when working on a horizontal directional drilling machine and proposed $165,514 in penalties. The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Maine Department of Labor announces October workplace safety and labor law training schedule

September 24, 2026

For Immediate Release: Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor offers free workplace safety and labor law training to help employers, managers, supervisors, human resources professionals and others understand workplace safety requirements and Maine labor laws. The Department has announced its schedule of October classes, with trainings offered through SafetyWorks! and the Bureau of Labor Standards.

Registration is required, and space may be limited. View the October schedule and register for a class.

Unless otherwise noted, classes are held at the SafetyWorks! Training Institute at the Maine Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive in Augusta.

October Class Schedule

Fire Extinguisher/Emergency Action Plans/Workplace Violence Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

entry.title: US Department of Labor releases new workplace guidance to prepare employers, workers for opioid emergencies
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration today released a fact sheet to help employers and workers rapidly respond to opioid-related overdose emergencies in the workplace.Opioid emergencies can happen anywhere, including at work, and being prepared can help save a life. OSHA’s new guidance, “Opioid Overdose Rescue with Reversal Medications,” is part of the Great American Recovery Initiative, a government-wide effort by the Trump Administration prioritizing addiction treatment and recovery. The fact sheet provides practical information that focuses on empowering workplaces to recognize the signs of an overdose and act immediately.“President Trump has charged the Department of Labor with making recovery part of our workforce strategy, helping more individuals return to work and ensuring our businesses have the workers they need,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Today’s guidance, released as part of President Trump’s Great American Recovery Initiative, is exactly the kind of action we were tasked with delivering on for the American people.”“President Trump has been fighting back against the deadly synthetic opioids infecting the entire illicit drug supply, from known illicit drugs to counterfeit tablets sold on the street or through fake online pharmacies,” said White House Drug Czar Sara Carter. “Because fentanyl has infiltrated the illicit drug landscape and acts as a chemical weapon against our people, it is critically important that the American workforce is familiar with drug overdose recognition and reversal. I am grateful to the Department of Labor for informing employers and workers about life-saving overdose reversal treatments like naloxone.”OSHA’s fact sheet highlights key opioid overdose preparedness strategies, including:Keep lifesaving FDA-approved reversal medications – such as naloxone or nalmefene – on hand. These safe, life-saving medications quickly restore normal breathing and generally have no effect if opioids are not present.Treat overdose kits like first aid by storing them in highly visible, easily accessible locations, just like automated external defibrillators or standard first-aid kits.Educate workers on how to identify critical symptoms of an overdose, such as slow or stopped breathing, blue lips or skin, pinpoint pupils, or unresponsiveness.Prepare for rapid action in an emergency by training workers to administer the medication, safely position the individual, and provide supportive care while waiting for first responders.OSHA’s guidance emphasizes that while these medications are critical, they do not replace emergency services. Workplace responders should always call 911 immediately because the medication’s effects are temporary and professional medical care is still required.The Department of Labor is committed to supporting workers’ safety and health on the job, along with partners at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and other agencies.Read the Opioid Overdose Rescue with Reversal Medications fact sheet.Learn more about OSHA.

entry.title: Maine CDC Shares Respiratory Virus Season Reminders
entry.content:
Sep 25, 2026

As fall arrives in Maine, respiratory viruses such as influenza (flu), COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), also return and begin to spread more widely as people spend more time together, indoors. The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) reminds Maine people and visitors to take steps to keep themselves, their loved ones, and neighbors healthy this respiratory virus season.

Respiratory viruses can cause fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle aches, and fatigue. Some people are more likely to get very sick and need medical attention. These viruses can spread when an infected person coughs or sneezes. They can also spread from touching the surface with the virus on it and then touching your nose or mouth before washing your hands.

The Maine CDC recommends the following measures to protect yourself and others:

  • Stay home when you are sick.
  • Wash your hands frequently with soap and water.
  • Clean and disinfect surfaces and objects that people touch often.
  • If you are sick, consider wearing a mask around others.
  • Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or your elbow.
  • Avoid close contact with people who are sick.
  • Get vaccinated, as appropriate for flu, COVID-19, and RSV.

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent respiratory viruses. Vaccines can also help make illness less severe and help prevent missed work or school. Getting a flu vaccine every year and staying up to date with COVID-19 and RSV vaccinations, if eligible, can help lower the risk of getting sick.

Consistent with the recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, the Maine CDC recommends the following respiratory virus immunization for the 2026-2027 season:

  • Flu: Everyone 6 months and older should receive an annual flu vaccine.
  • COVID-19: Vaccination is recommended for
    • all children ages 6 through 23 months;
    • children and adolescents ages 2 through 18 years who are at increased risk for severe COVID-19 or who want to be vaccinated;
    • adults age 19 and older;
    • pregnant individuals.
  • RSV: Immunization is recommended for certain infants, pregnant people, and older adults.
    • Infants: RSV immunization is recommended for those younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, if they are not protected by maternal RSV vaccination.
      • Certain children ages 8-19 months who are at increased risk for severe RSV may also be recommended to receive RSV immunization during their second season.
    • Pregnant people: RSV vaccination is recommended during weeks 32 through 36 of pregnancy.
    • Older adults: All adults age 75 and older and adults 50-74 at increased risk for severe RSV illness.

To find the nearest location to get a vaccine, contact your local pharmacy or health care provider.

entry.title: Disability Employment Awareness Month - October
entry.content:
WHEREAS, October 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of National Disability Employment Awareness Month; and

WHEREAS, workplaces across our state that are welcoming of the talents of all people, including people with disabilities, are critical to healthy communities and a strong economy; and

WHEREAS, while the employment rate of people with disabilities ages 16 to 64 in Maine has increased to 44 percent, it remains significantly lower than the 83 percent employment rate for Maine people without disabilities; and

WHEREAS, it is important that the State of Maine prepare all youth, including those with disabilities, for meaningful careers and an adulthood that includes employment; and

WHEREAS, Maine is an Employment First state, affirming employment as the first and preferred option for people with disabilities who receive services from state agencies; and

WHEREAS, people with disabilities, including people who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing, Late Deafened, Blind or with Low Vision make significant contributions to Maine's economy and communities; and

WHEREAS, activities during this month will reinforce the value and talent people with disabilities add to our workplaces and communities and affirm Maine's commitment to increasing access to good jobs and competitive, integrated employment for all workers, including those with disabilities;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as 

Disability Employment Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I call upon employers, schools, higher education institutions and other community organizations in Maine to observe October with appropriate programs and activities that celebrate the contributions of people with disabilities and promote access to good, in-demand jobs and career pathways such as registered apprenticeships for all Maine people.

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty eighth day of

September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

entry.title: US Labor Department obtains court order naming independent fiduciary for 401(k) plan of defunct WA-based aerospace company
entry.content: SEATTLE – The U.S. Department of Labor has secured a court order to appoint an independent fiduciary to manage the abandoned 401(k) plan of a defunct Arlington-based aerospace company.The order, entered in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, appoints AMI Benefit Plan Administrators Inc. as the independent fiduciary for the Commercial Aircraft Interiors LLC 401(k) Plan, which has been frozen since the employer shut down operations in 2023. In this role, the independent fiduciary will be able to distribute its assets to eligible former employees who have not been able to access their retirement savings because the only responsive company representative, Charles Pratt, lacked the legal authority needed to approve distributions. The independent fiduciary will also be able to formally terminate the plan.“The appointment of an independent fiduciary will give the participants in the Commercial Aircraft Interiors plan access to the funds that rightly belong to them,” said Liam Roberts, district director for the department’s Employee Benefits Security Administration in Seattle. “We urge all workers to contact the department for assistance when their retirement plan has been abandoned and they have not received the benefits to which they are entitled.”Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, all employee benefit plans are required to be managed by named fiduciaries. Without one, participants and beneficiaries cannot get information about their accounts or collect retirement benefits. The Commercial Aircraft Interiors plan has approximately $260,000 in assets and 59 participants.EBSA ensures the security of retirement, health, and other job-based benefits for American workers and their families. The agency is responsible for protecting more than 155 million workers, retirees, and their families, who are covered by approximately 2.8 million health plans, 837,000 private retirement plans, and 521,000 additional welfare benefit plans. Together, these plans hold about $15.2 trillion in assets.Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

entry.title: Former union officials charged with wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud for embezzling approximately $350K in member funds over 5 years
entry.content: CLEVELAND – An investigation by the U.S. Department of Labor has led to criminal charges for two former union officials who allegedly embezzled approximately $350,000 from the union members they swore to serve.An investigation by the department’s Office of Labor-Management Standards in Cleveland found that the former president and secretary-treasurer of the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees Local 1746 conspired to access the union’s finances for unauthorized transactions for their personal benefit from 2017 to 2022.Criminal charges were filed this month in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio against the union’s former President Pamela Brown and former Secretary-Treasurer Adelle Burrell-Williams. The charging documents allege these former officers used the union’s debit card to withdraw cash at casinos and wrote unauthorized checks from the union’s operating account. The department also alleges that Brown and Burrell-Williams attempted to avoid detection by creating false reports and failing to maintain financial records. The union lost approximately $350,000 as a result of Brown and Burrell-Williams’ actions. The former union officials were responsible for overseeing the union, managing its finances, paying authorized expenses, maintaining financial records, and creating financial reports during their tenures as principal officers of Local 1746, a union representing 1,200 employees at Cuyahoga County Health and Human Services.The prosecution of this case is being handled by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio.Criminal complaints, or the filing of an information, are charges only and are not evidence of guilt. Each defendant is entitled to a fair trial in which it is the government’s burden to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Labor union fraud such as embezzlement, filing false reports, maintaining false records, destroying or concealing records, and other criminal activity can be reported by email to OLMS-Public@dol.gov, to the OLMS National Office at 202-693-0143, or to your local OLMS field office. MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Oct 01, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Program Publishes Actuarial Report, First Claims Report

October 1, 2026

For Immediate Release: Oct. 1, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

Actuarial report projects PFML Trust Fund will remain stable for the next 10 years

AUGUSTA - The Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) program has published its second annual actuarial report, as well as its first claims report on Oct. 1, 2026.

PFML became law in 2023 and is a statewide program that provides eligible workers with up to 12 weeks of paid leave for medical, parental, family care, military family or safe leave.

The PFML program began accepting claims on March 30, 2026, and began paying benefits on May 1, 2026. This initial claims report covers the program's first three months of claims activity, from March 30 through June 30, 2026. Future claims reports will be published annually and will cover a full year of claims activity.

Highlights of the reports include:

  • The PFML Trust Fund remains solvent and based on updated revenue and claim expenditure, is projected to remain stable for the next 10 years.
  • The program received 8,376 applications between March 30 and June 30, 2026.
  • Among the claims approved, medical leave was the most common reason, followed by welcoming a new child and caring for a family member. Other leave reasons represented a very small portion of the overall claim volume.

"We are excited to see the PFML Program effectively off the ground and helping Maine workers and businesses through life's big moments, both now and for years to come," said PFML Director Luke Monahan.

More information on the PFML program, including how to apply, can be found on the program's website: https://www.maine.gov/paidleave/

Employees, employers and self-employed individuals with questions can call 207-621-5024 between8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. Employees can send a message through the Benefits Application Portal, while employers and self-employed individuals can send a message through the Maine Paid Leave Contributions Portal.

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - Gov. Janet T. Mills has proclaimed October 2026 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM).

October 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of NDEAM. Gov. Mills' proclamation recognizes the contributions of people with disabilities to Maine's workplaces, communities and economy and calls on employers, schools, higher education institutions and community organizations to promote access to good, in-demand jobs and career pathways, including registered apprenticeship.

"At a time when employers are searching for workers, talented Maine people with disabilities are ready and willing to participate in the workforce," said Jennifer Kimble, the chair of Maine's Commission on Disability and Employment. "Expanding recruitment and retention strategies that recognize the value of including workers with disabilities as benefits businesses, communities, and the individuals whose talents are too often underutilized."

The Commission on Disability and Employment was established by the legislature in 1997 and promotes collaboration with the public and private sectors to increase awareness and influence policy related to employment for people with disabilities. Its members envision a Maine workforce that includes all people with disabilities employed in jobs that meet both their economic and personal needs.

"National Disability Employment Awareness Month is an opportunity to recognize the skills, talents and contributions of Mainers with disabilities and to continue working toward workplaces where everyone has the opportunity to contribute and succeed," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Maine's workforce needs every person who wants to work, and the Department of Labor and our partners are committed to helping people with disabilities pursue meaningful careers while helping employers connect with talented workers."

NDEAM has been observed nationally since 1945. The observance recognizes the contributions of people with disabilities and promotes employment opportunities and career pathways.

entry.title: US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather
entry.content: LITTLE ROCK, AR – A U.S. Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. violated the Federal Railroad Safety Act when it removed from service and later terminated a North Little Rock yardman who notified management of nearby lightning and federal safety standards. OSHA determined that the employee voiced concerns about nearby lightning, cited OSHA and NOAA lightening safety guidelines, initiated a safety stand-down, and refused to work until the storm passed. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. Union Pacific terminated his employment on May 30, 2024.On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees. Union Pacific filed objections to OSHA’s order and has requested a hearing before a U.S. Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge.OSHA’s Whistleblower Protection Program enforces 25 whistleblower statutes that protect employees from retaliation for reporting violations of workplace airline, anti-money laundering, commercial motor carrier, consumer product, criminal antitrust, environmental, financial reform, food safety, health insurance reform, maritime, motor vehicle safety, nuclear, pipeline, public transportation agency, railroad, safety and health, securities, and tax laws.Editor’s note: The U.S. Department of Labor does not release the names of employees involved in whistleblower complaints.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $10.2 million to 67 organizations to promote workplace safety and health training
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration today announced the award approximately $10.2 million in grant funds to 67 organizations across the nation to support education and training focused on worker safety to help employees and employers recognize serious workplace hazards and employ safety and health programs.Funded through the Susan Harwood Training Grant Program, the grants aim to advance worker safety and health by providing instructor-led training opportunities for workers and employers in small businesses with an emphasis on industries with high injury, illness, and fatality rates.The grants will fund training and education on hazard awareness, prevention, and controls to protect workers from on-the-job hazards through the development of quality classroom-ready training and educational materials that identify and prevent workplace hazards.The grants honor the legacy and work of Dr. Susan Harwood who, during her 17 years with OSHA, developed workplace safety guidelines for benzene, formaldehyde, bloodborne pathogens and lead in the construction industry. Harwood was also primary author of OSHA’s cotton dust standard which virtually eliminated byssinosis – a lung disease that causes asthma-like symptoms – among textile workers.Learn more about the Susan Harwood Training Grant Program and 2026 awardees.

To Providers of Adult or Children's Services to Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ID) or Autism

Oct 02, 2026

The State of Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) is planning to launch the new Lifespan Waiver in May 2027. 

Our first priority is to offer support for future providers of Lifespan services.  Following our Lifespan Provider Readiness project in 2025, we are reaching out to understand provider interest in offering services under Lifespan. To that end, we created a survey to gauge interest from providers who serve individuals fourteen or older who have ID or autism. 

Please take a few minutes to complete this survey. 

The survey will be open until Friday, October 16, at 4:00 PM.
